title_en: Shanghai International Trust and Investment Co., Ltd. v. Shanghai Comprehensive Information Exchange and Shanghai Sanhe Real Estate Company — dispute over entrusted loan contract
ruling_gist_en: Article 39 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If the parties to the main contract agree to repay the old loan with a new loan, the surety shall not bear civil liability unless the surety knew or should have known. If the new loan and the old loan have the same surety, the preceding paragraph shall not apply." Accordingly, where the parties to a loan contract, based on an agreement to repay the old loan with a new loan, successively conclude multiple loan contracts, and the same guarantor, who should have known, affixes its seal to these multiple loan contracts to consent to the guarantee, it shall bear the guarantee liability in accordance with the law. If the guarantor denies the contractual nature of repaying the old loan with a new loan on the ground that there is no formal or intrinsic connection among the multiple loan contracts, and thus refuses to perform the guarantee liability, the people's court shall not support such a defense.

full_text_en:
Shanghai International Trust and Investment Co., Ltd. v. Shanghai Comprehensive Information Exchange and Shanghai Sanhe Real Estate Company — dispute over entrusted loan contract

Ruling Summary

Article 39 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China stipulates: "Where the parties to the principal contract agree to repay an old loan with a new loan, the guarantor shall not bear civil liability unless the guarantor knew or should have known of such arrangement. Where the guarantor for the new loan and the old loan is the same person, the preceding paragraph shall not apply." Accordingly, where the parties to a loan contract, based on a mutual agreement to repay an old loan with a new loan, successively enter into multiple loan contracts, and the same guarantor, in circumstances where it should have known, affixes its seal to agree to provide guarantee on such multiple loan contracts, it shall bear guarantee liability in accordance with law. Where the guarantor denies the nature of the contract as a repayment of an old loan with a new loan on the ground that there is no formal or intrinsic connection between the multiple loan contracts, and thereby refuses to perform the guarantee liability, the people's court shall not support such argument.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2005) Min Er Ti Zi No. 8

Applicant for Retrial (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Shanghai Sanhe Real Estate Company, domiciled at No. 358 Yan'an West Road, Shanghai.

Legal Representative: Gu Jianguo, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Gao Yuying, lawyer of Beijing Century Law Firm, Shanghai Branch.

Agent ad litem: Liu Hui, General Manager of the Company.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Shanghai International Trust and Investment Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 111 Jiujiang Road, Shanghai.

Legal Representative: Zhou Youdao, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Fang Xiaomei, lawyer of Kangda Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Chen Zhiwei, lawyer of Kangda Law Firm, Shanghai Branch.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Shanghai Comprehensive Information Exchange, domiciled at Room 806, No. 137 Jiujiang Road, Shanghai.

Legal Representative: Song Xinhua, Manager of the Exchange.

Agent ad litem: Song Rongsheng, Director of the Office of the Exchange.

Shanghai Sanhe Real Estate Company (hereinafter referred to as Sanhe Company), in connection with the dispute over an entrusted loan contract with Shanghai International Trust and Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shangguotou) and Shanghai Comprehensive Information Exchange (hereinafter referred to as the Exchange), refused to accept the civil judgment (2001) Hu Gao Jing Zai Zhong Zi No. 19 of the Shanghai High People's Court and applied to this Court for retrial. This Court, by the civil ruling (2002) Min Er Jian Zi No. 110-1 dated June 23, 2005, decided to conduct a retrial of this case. This Court held a public hearing in accordance with law. Gao Yuying and Liu Hui, agents ad litem of Sanhe Company, Fang Xiaomei and Chen Zhiwei, agents ad litem of Shangguotou, and Song Rongsheng, agent ad litem of the Exchange, appeared before the court for the proceedings. This case is now concluded.

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court found at first instance: During the period from January 10, 1996 to April 6, 1998, Shangguotou and the Exchange entered into a total of five entrusted loan contracts, numbered sequentially by time as 922660, 922790, 922804, 922805, and 300263. Each loan amount was RMB 20 million, with monthly interest rates of 7.89‰, 6.9‰, and 6.435‰ respectively. The purpose of the loans was for material purchase deposit or working capital turnover. The guarantor for all contracts was Sanhe Company. Shangguotou disbursed the loans to the Exchange as agreed. The off-case client, Shanghai Shangtou Investment Management Co., Ltd., only affixed its official seal on the last two entrusted loan contracts. All five entrusted loan contracts involved a repayment of old loans with new loans. After the maturity of the loan under the last contract No. 300263, the Exchange repaid only RMB 2,278,000 of the principal and RMB 600,000 of overdue loan interest, leaving an outstanding principal of RMB 17,722,000, interest during the term of RMB 789,454.95, and corresponding overdue interest. Shangguotou requested the court of first instance to order the Exchange to repay the loan principal and interest, and Sanhe Company to bear joint and several liability for the Exchange's repayment obligation.

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court held at first instance: The entrusted loan contracts numbered 922660, 922790, 922804, and 922805, entered into between Shangguotou, the Exchange, and Sanhe Company, reflected the true intentions of the parties and were legally valid. Since these four contracts had all been fully performed, they were no longer to be dealt with. The entrusted loan contract numbered 300263, entered into between Shangguotou, the Exchange, and Sanhe Company, was legally valid, and all parties were bound to abide by it. Shangguotou had fulfilled its loan disbursement obligation as agreed. The Exchange, having only repaid part of the loan principal and overdue interest, failed to repay the remaining loan principal and interest, which constituted a clear breach of contract. The Exchange should bear the responsibility of repaying the outstanding loan principal, interest during the term, and corresponding overdue interest under the disputed contract, and Sanhe Company should bear joint and several guarantee liability. Sanhe Company argued that it was unaware that the loan under the disputed contract was used to repay an old loan, and thus should not bear the guarantee liability for that loan. Since the guarantor for the disputed contract and the other four related entrusted loan contracts was Sanhe Company, Sanhe Company's guarantee liability had not been expanded due to its alleged ignorance of the repayment of old loans with new loans, and therefore Sanhe Company's guarantee liability could not be discharged. Sanhe Company further argued that the nature and purpose of the five entrusted loan contracts differed, that the contracts did not indicate a loan-to-loan repayment, and that the relationship between the five contracts could not be proven. However, based on the identity of the contracting parties, the loan amounts, and other content, it was factually established that the five contracts involved a repayment of old loans with new loans, so Sanhe Company's argument was not accepted. Sanhe Company's claim that Shangguotou and the Exchange had maliciously colluded to induce Sanhe Company to provide a guarantee in order to transfer risk was merely a unilateral inference lacking factual basis, and was not recognized. The court ruled: 1. The Exchange shall repay to Shangguotou the loan principal of RMB 17,722,000, interest during the term of RMB 789,454.95, and overdue loan interest of RMB 1,626,712.54 within ten days from the effective date of this judgment; 2. The Exchange shall repay to Shangguotou the overdue loan interest from November 20, 1999 to the effective date of this judgment within ten days from the effective date of this judgment; 3. Sanhe Company shall bear joint and several liability for the Exchange's repayment obligations under items 1 and 2 above. The case acceptance fee of RMB 112,919 shall be borne jointly by the Exchange and Sanhe Company.

Sanhe Company, refusing to accept the judgment of first instance, appealed to the Shanghai High People's Court.

The Shanghai High People's Court found at second instance: The disputed contract No. 300263 was signed on April 6, 1998, with a loan amount of RMB 20 million. Shangguotou disbursed the loan on the same day but immediately deducted the full amount internally to repay the loan under contract No. 922805 signed on October 10, 1997. Contract No. 922805 and the related contracts No. 922804 signed on December 31, 1996, and No. 922790 signed on July 10, 1996, had no disbursement records or internal deduction records. The earliest guarantee provided by Sanhe Company for Shangguotou and the Exchange was for contract No. 922660 dated January 10, 1996. On January 11, 1996, Shangguotou disbursed RMB 20 million to the Exchange and deducted RMB 10 million of principal on the same day. Within the two days of January 10 to 11, 1996, Shangguotou disbursed a total of RMB 32 million to the Exchange (including RMB 12 million in dispute in another case), and deducted a total of RMB 30 million of principal.

The court further found: On November 28, 1996, the Exchange entered into an agreement with Jiangsu Xishan Hongsheng Town Industrial General Company (hereinafter referred to as Hongsheng Company), which stated that from March 1, 1994 to June 10, 1996, the Exchange had lent a total of RMB 30.4 million to Hongsheng Company, with an outstanding balance of RMB 25 million as of December 1995. During the trial, the Exchange stated that the above funds were borrowed from Shangguotou. After the judgment of first instance, on October 30, 2000, the Exchange sent a letter to Hongsheng Company stating: "Regarding the amount your company owes us, in accordance with the lawsuit filed by Shanghai International Trust and Investment Company on November 10, 1999 with the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, the case was concluded on October 25, 2000, and a judgment was rendered. From 1994 to the present, in the spirit of assisting your town's construction and development, we have successively paid you principal of RMB 27,497,261.15 and overdue interest of RMB 7,019,685.48, totaling RMB 34,516,946.63 (excluding interest for 2000). We require your company to actively cooperate with us in repaying the loan promptly." It was also found that before January 10, 1996, the guarantors for all loans from Shangguotou to the Exchange were not Sanhe Company, but the off-case parties Shanghai Materials Cooperation Development Company and China Foreign Exchange Trading Center. Among the funds lent by the Exchange to Hongsheng Company, RMB 19.15 million was directly remitted by Shangguotou to Hongsheng Company.

The Shanghai High People's Court held at second instance: The court of first instance's findings and judgment regarding the existence of a creditor-debtor relationship between Shangguotou and the Exchange were correct and should be upheld. However, the court of first instance failed to ascertain the formation process of the creditor-debtor relationship between Shangguotou and the Exchange, and the fact that Sanhe Company provided the guarantee without knowledge of the pre-existing creditor-debtor relationship between Shangguotou and the Exchange. From the facts found at second instance, it was clear that a creditor-debtor relationship arising from loans had long existed between Shangguotou and the Exchange, and the guarantors for the earlier loan contracts were not Sanhe Company. The performance of the five loan contracts for which Sanhe Company provided guarantees to Shangguotou and the Exchange either involved same-day borrowing and repayment, or empty loans with no disbursement records. The risk of non-recovery of loans due to Shangguotou's lending had already arisen before Sanhe Company provided the guarantee, i.e., before January 10, 1996. Shangguotou and the Exchange jointly concealed the true situation of repaying old loans with new loans, induced Sanhe Company to provide the guarantee, and transferred the guarantee liability that should have been borne by others to Sanhe Company. Pursuant to Article 30 of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 39 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, Sanhe Company should not bear the guarantee liability. The court of first instance's judgment regarding Sanhe Company's guarantee liability was incorrect and should be reversed. The court ruled: 1. Affirm items 1 and 2 of the first-instance judgment; 2. Reverse item 3 of the first-instance judgment. The case acceptance fee of RMB 112,919 for first instance shall be borne by the Exchange, and the case acceptance fee of RMB 112,919 for second instance shall be borne by Shangguotou.

Shangguotou, refusing to accept the second-instance judgment, applied to the Shanghai High People's Court for retrial.

The Shanghai High People's Court found upon retrial: On the date of disbursement of the loan under contract No. 300263, Shangguotou made the disbursement in accordance with the Exchange's payment instruction. The second instance's finding of fact on this point was erroneous, but the remainder of its factual findings were correct. It was further found that since 1996, Sanhe Company and the Exchange had each borrowed from Shangguotou and provided mutual guarantees for each other. On December 7, 2001, with the approval of the Shanghai Administration for Industry and Commerce, Shangguotou changed its name to Shanghai International Trust and Investment Co., Ltd.

The Shanghai High People's Court held upon retrial: In chronological order, between January 10, 1996 and April 6, 1998, Shangguotou and the Exchange entered into entrusted loan contracts numbered 922660, 922790, 922804, 922805, and 300263. All five contracts were valid, each with a loan amount of RMB 20 million, a purpose of material purchase deposit and working capital turnover, and with Sanhe Company as the guarantor. Among them, contracts 922660 and 300263 had disbursement and deduction records, but the Exchange did not dispute the borrowing. Therefore, the other three contracts should be regarded as extensions of contract 922660. For contract 300263, Shangguotou, on the day of disbursement and in accordance with the Exchange's instruction, used the "new loan" to repay the "old loan" under contract 922805. Shangguotou fulfilled its obligations under contract 300263 as agreed. The Exchange, as the borrower, only repaid part of the principal and interest, which constituted a breach of contract, and should repay the outstanding principal, interest during the term, and overdue interest to Shangguotou. Although the guarantors for contracts before 922660 were off-case parties, not Sanhe Company, the principal debts under those pre-922660 contracts were extinguished by the repayment of old loans with new loans under contract 922660. Contracts 922790, 922804, and 922805, as extensions of contracts 922660, 922790, and 922804 respectively, had their principal debts extinguished by the repayment of old loans with new loans under contract 300263. Pursuant to Article 39 of the Judicial Interpretation on the Guarantee Law: "Where the parties to the principal contract agree to repay an old loan with a new loan, the guarantor shall not bear civil liability unless the guarantor knew or should have known of such arrangement. Where the guarantor for the new loan and the old loan is the same person, the preceding paragraph shall not apply." In this case, the guarantor Sanhe Company had provided multiple guarantees for the Exchange's loans, and the Exchange had also provided guarantees for Sanhe Company's loans from Shangguotou (mutual guarantees). The second instance failed to find that Sanhe Company, as the guarantor of the disputed contract 300263, "should have known" that the loans between Shangguotou and the Exchange involved repayment of old loans with new loans, and this should be corrected. Moreover, Sanhe Company was simultaneously the guarantor for the unperformed contract 300263 (new loan) and the performed contract 922805 (old loan), and thus the second paragraph of Article 39 of the Judicial Interpretation on the Guarantee Law should apply. Sanhe Company's claim that the risk of non-repayment existed before it became the guarantor, and that its guarantee was the result of malicious collusion and inducing guarantee between Shangguotou and the Exchange, lacked sufficient basis. Sanhe Company should bear the guarantee liability for the disputed loan contract. Pursuant to Article 18 of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 39, paragraph 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 184, paragraph 1 and 153, paragraph 1, items (2) and (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and after discussion by the Judicial Committee, the court ruled: 1. Set aside the civil judgment (2000) Hu Gao Jing Zhong Zi No. 588 of this court. 2. Affirm the civil judgment (1999) Hu Er Zhong Jing Chu Zi No. 811 of the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 112,919 shall be borne jointly by the Exchange and Sanhe Company.

Sanhe Company, refusing to accept the retrial judgment of the Shanghai High People's Court, applied to this Court for retrial.

Sanhe Company's grounds for retrial: Among the five loan contracts guaranteed by Sanhe Company, only the first and fifth contracts had actual disbursement and deduction; the second, third, and fourth contracts had no actual disbursement and were empty loans. The deduction under the disputed fifth contract actually repaid the old loan under the first contract, which itself was used to repay an old loan with a new loan. However, the guarantor for the earlier old loan was not Sanhe Company, and the first contract was signed more than two years before the fifth contract. Since Shangguotou did not claim against the Exchange for more than two years, Sanhe Company's guarantee liability should also be discharged. The purpose of the disputed fifth contract was working capital, while the other four contracts were for purchase contract deposits. There was no formal or intrinsic connection indicating a repayment of old loans with new loans. There was no fact of mutual guarantees between Sanhe Company and the Exchange. The Exchange also admitted that it did not inform Sanhe Company of the "repayment of old loans with new loans" arrangement. Inferring that the applicant should have known of the "repayment with new loans" had no factual or legal basis. The retrial judgment, while affirming that the second instance's factual findings were basically correct, made an opposite ruling on whether the guarantor should bear guarantee liability, lacking evidentiary support and legal basis.

Shangguotou responded: The guarantor for all five loan contracts was Sanhe Company. Although the guarantors for contracts before 922660 were off-case parties, the principal debts under those contracts were extinguished by the repayment of old loans with new loans under contract 922660. Contracts 922790, 922804, and 922805, as extensions of contracts 922660, 922790, and 922804 respectively, had their principal debts extinguished by the repayment of old loans with new loans under contract 300263. The five loan contracts were continuous. Moreover, from 1993 to 1998, the Exchange provided guarantees for a large number of loans from Shangguotou to Sanhe Company, and there were numerous mutual guarantee operations between the two parties. Sanhe Company should have known of the repayment of old loans with new loans, and its guarantee liability should not be discharged.

The Exchange did not submit a written statement. At the trial, it stated: The loan under contract 300263 was used to repay the principal and interest under contract 922805.

This Court found upon retrial: Article 6 of the first four entrusted loan contracts all stipulated: "Upon maturity of the loan, if the Exchange cannot repay on time and needs to renew the loan, it must obtain the written consent of Shangguotou, pay off the interest, and Shangguotou shall handle the new entrusted loan procedures as a new borrowing." Article 6 of the fifth contract was substantially similar, except that "need to renew the loan" was amended to "need to extend the loan." Sanhe Company affixed its official seal on all five loan contracts. Apart from the same loan amount, starting from the second contract, each subsequent contract was signed when the previous contract matured, and its term essentially connected with the maturity of the loan to be repaid. Under the first contract 922660, on the day the RMB 20 million loan was disbursed, Shangguotou deducted RMB 10 million of principal to repay the Exchange's old loan guaranteed by off-case parties, and the remaining RMB 10 million was used by the Exchange. After the second contract 922790 was signed, Shangguotou used the method of replacing loan certificates to repay the loan under the first contract with the loan under the second contract. The operation for the third and fourth contracts was the same as the second. Under the fifth contract 300263, on the day the loan was disbursed, Shangguotou deducted the amount on the same day in accordance with the Exchange's payment instruction to repay the loan under the fourth contract 922805. The Exchange consistently acknowledged Shangguotou's claim for repayment of principal and interest under contract 300263, and also admitted that it did not inform Sanhe Company that the first loan had been used to repay the loan guaranteed by off-case parties. This Court confirms the other facts found by the Shanghai High People's Court upon retrial.

Opinion of this Court upon Retrial: The determination by the Shanghai High People's Court upon retrial regarding the validity of the contracts in this case and the Exchange's liability for breach of contract is correct, and this Court supports it upon retrial. The contracts involved in this case are titled as entrusted loan contracts, but the parties in this case did not allege the facts of entrusted loans; therefore, the nature of the case should be loan and guarantee contracts. It is true that there were instances of no actual disbursement of funds among the five contracts in this case, but such instances arose from the agreement in Article 6 of the contracts between the borrower and the lender. From the content of that article, and the fact that the loan amounts for the new and old loans were identical and the loan periods were essentially consecutive, it can be seen that when the old loan was due but not yet repaid, the purpose of the borrower and lender in entering into the new loan contract was precisely to repay the old loan with the new loan and extinguish the borrower's debt under the old loan. That article can be regarded as an agreement between the borrower and lender on borrowing new loans to repay old loans. The practice of Shangguotou in deducting the loan on the same day it was disbursed or merely replacing the loan certificate without actual disbursement was a performance act based on the agreement in the contract to borrow new loans to repay old loans, and is also the basic method of performance for borrowing new loans to repay old loans. Sanhe Company consecutively affixed its seal to several loan contracts, agreeing to act as guarantor for the Exchange. It should have known that this was a way for the contracting parties to perform the agreement in Article 6 of the contract, i.e., borrowing new loans to repay old loans. The terms of the contracts in this case did not violate any prohibitive provisions of the law, and Sanhe Company confirmed by affixing its seal. Therefore, this case should apply the provisions of Article 39 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues Concerning the Application of the Guaranty Law of the People's Republic of China regarding borrowing new loans to repay old loans. If, as Sanhe Company claims, this case does not involve borrowing new loans to repay old loans, and if the inference is drawn that there is no formal or intrinsic connection between the five contracts, then Sanhe Company would bear guarantee liability not for one contract but for the cumulative amount of RMB 100 million under the five contracts. Sanhe Company's arguments that the loan purpose lacks the form and intrinsic connection of borrowing new to repay old, and that the three intermediate contracts had no actual disbursement, thereby denying that this is borrowing new to repay old, are untenable. Moreover, prior to and after the signing of the contracts in this case, Sanhe Company, as a borrower, had multiple loans from Shangguotou, with the Exchange acting as guarantor. The basic format of those loan contracts between Sanhe Company and Shangguotou was identical to that of the contracts in this case, and the method of performance, involving short-term deductions or replacement of certificates, was also the same as the performance method in this case. Therefore, Sanhe Company's defense that it should not be deemed to have known that such an agreement in this case constituted borrowing new loans to repay old loans lacks reasonableness.

Starting from Contract No. 300263 in this case and tracing back, Sanhe Company was the guarantor for four consecutive loan contracts. It has thus lost the conditions for exemption from guarantor liability under Article 39 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues Concerning the Application of the Guaranty Law of the People's Republic of China. Paragraph 2 of that article clearly states: "If the new loan and the old loan have the same guarantor, the provisions of the preceding paragraph shall not apply." As the same guarantor for both the new and old loans, Sanhe Company's claim that it should be exempted from guarantee liability on the grounds that it did not know or should not have known that the principal contract involved borrowing new loans to repay old loans is not supported by this Court. The determination in the first-instance judgment that, because Contract No. 300263 involved borrowing new to repay old, Contracts No. 922660, 922790, 922804, and 922805 had been fully performed by the new loan repaying the old loan, that Shangguotou had performed its loan disbursement obligation as agreed, that the Exchange had not yet repaid the principal and interest under Contract No. 300263 and should bear liability for breach of contract, and that Sanhe Company should bear joint and several guarantee liability, was correctly affirmed by the Shanghai High People's Court upon retrial, and this Court also affirms it upon retrial. In summary, pursuant to Item (1) of Paragraph 1 of Article 153 and Paragraph 1 of Article 186 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

We affirm the civil judgment of the Shanghai High People's Court, (2001) Hu Gao Jing Zai Zhong Zi No. 19.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Tan Hong

Judge: He Ti

Acting Judge: Wang Yunfei

August 13, 2008

Clerk: Liu Yuanyuan
